title: The $110 Billion Mirage — GAO Audit vs. DOGE's Wall of Receipts
narrative: DOGE — the Department of Government Efficiency, which was never an official department and wound down last month — publicly claimed $110 billion in savings via its 'Wall of Receipts' website covering contracts, grants, and leases. By its own tally, DOGE claimed roughly $214 billion in total cuts. Elon Musk, who led DOGE until May 2025, originally promised as much as $2 trillion a year in federal savings. On Thursday, the Government Accountability Office released its audit. The finding: DOGE could not verify the calculation method behind 96% of reported savings. Thousands of 'terminated' contracts were never touched. More than a hundred leases DOGE claimed credit for ending were already in the process of expiring. The Wall of Receipts was a wall of aspiration — and the audit trail was public the whole time.
telemetry: DOGE claimed $110bn in savings via 'Wall of Receipts' website; $214bn in cuts overall by its own estimate
Elon Musk original promise: 'as much as $2tn a year' in federal savings
GAO report (Thu 6 Aug): several savings estimates 'incorrect or lack supporting evidence'; 'several issues limit the transparency and reliability of these reported savings'
GAO: could not verify calculation method behind 96% of DOGE-reported savings
108 of 264 leases DOGE identified for termination were already ending before DOGE existed — erasing ~$15.3m of $53.5m in real lease savings (DOGE claimed $113m for lease cuts)
2,503 of 13,476 contracts DOGE claimed it terminated had 'no termination action' taken
$1.7bn Department of Defence IT-services contract DOGE credited as savings 'was never terminated' — zero savings achieved
DOGE did not respond to GAO requests for information and interviews
White House response: 'all employees had to complete ethics training and follow financial disclosure requirements' — no substantive rebuttal
Sens. Gary Peters (D-MI) and Richard Blumenthal (D-CT): 'DOGE was a slapdash and deceptive effort that misled the American people'
GAO compared DOGE claims against official federal databases (USASpending.gov, SAM.gov, GSA lease records) — every line item independently checkable
Even by DOGE's own website, claimed savings ($214bn) fall ~90% short of Musk's promised $2tn/year
analysis:
The GAO audit is devastating not because it finds errors — every large government initiative contains errors — but because it finds that 96% of DOGE's claimed savings cannot be verified at all. This is not an audit that says 'DOGE overcounted by 15%.' It is an audit that says DOGE provided no supporting evidence for nearly all of its claims, and for those claims where evidence exists, the evidence contradicts the claim.

The four most damaging findings, in order of severity:

First: the $1.7 billion phantom. DOGE claimed credit for terminating a Department of Defence IT-services contract and counted $1.7 billion in savings. The GAO found the contract was never terminated. Not 'terminated and then reinstated.' Not 'terminated with partial savings.' Never terminated. The $1.7 billion never existed as savings. It existed only as a line item on a website.

Second: the 2,503 contracts with 'no termination action.' DOGE claimed 13,476 contract terminations. The GAO checked federal contract databases and found nearly one in five — 2,503 — had no record of any termination action whatsoever. The contracts simply continued. DOGE counted them as savings anyway.

Third: the lease double-counting. DOGE claimed $113 million in lease savings from 264 terminations. The actual leases referenced summed to $53.5 million — less than half the claim. Of those, 108 leases were already in the process of ending before DOGE existed, wiping out another $15.3 million. The real, verifiable lease savings: roughly $38 million. DOGE claimed: $113 million. Inflated by 3x.

Fourth: the 96% black box. The GAO could not verify the calculation method behind 96% of DOGE-reported savings. This is not a detail. It is the entire claim. DOGE published a number — $110 billion — without a methodology that survives independent audit. When the GAO asked DOGE for information and interviews, DOGE did not respond.

The White House response — 'all employees had to complete ethics training' — is not a response to the audit. It is a non-sequitur. The question is whether the claimed savings are real. The answer, from the federal government's own auditor, is that 96% of them cannot be verified, and the verifiable 4% is riddled with phantom terminations, double-counting, and contracts that were never touched.

Musk's original promise of $2 trillion a year is worth revisiting in light of the audit. Even DOGE's own website — the most favorable possible accounting — shows $214 billion, roughly 10.7% of the target. The GAO audit suggests even that figure is inflated by an unknown but substantial margin. The gap between the promise and the reality is not a rounding error. It is two orders of magnitude.

The GAO compared DOGE's claims against official, publicly available federal databases — USASpending.gov, SAM.gov, GSA lease records. Every line item the GAO checked is checkable by any reporter or citizen with a web browser. The Wall of Receipts was not a secret. It was a public website making public claims, backed by public databases that contradicted them. Anyone could have run the same audit the GAO ran. The GAO simply had the institutional authority to make the findings official.
verdict: [SIPHONED VERDICT]: The Wall of Receipts was a wall of aspiration. 96% of DOGE's claimed savings cannot be verified. 2,503 'terminated' contracts were never touched — including a $1.7bn Defence contract DOGE claimed credit for that was never terminated at all. Lease savings were inflated by 3x. DOGE refused to cooperate with the GAO audit. The audit trail was public the whole time — USASpending.gov, SAM.gov, GSA records — and it contradicted the claims. Musk's original $2tn/year promise fell 90% short even by DOGE's own accounting. By the GAO's accounting, even that 10% is suspect.
